platform: Local Linux x86-64, glibc 2.36; archive floor 2.38. Lean 4.32.2, GCC/G++ 12.2.0, pkg-config 1.8.1 and CMake 3.31.6.
observations: Two separately built components per target: the first from ordinary Lean sources and the peer from those same nominal definitions plus an independently checked public Binding IR. Each consumer linked both relocated installs, first with pkg-config and then with CMake; neither consumer build used Lean or the producer sources.

Independent replay reinstalled the four retained archives without rebuilding their producers. Both clients passed again through pkg-config and CMake. The same unmodified C client also passed against the ordinary C package and the reviewed C++ peer. For each executable the loader resolved its component libraries to the intended relocated installs and loaded a single copy of each shared runtime library. The release CLI independently verified all four receipts.

Both components mutate and return the same Lean object. Retaining creates a separate, independently closeable lease; equal-valued objects remain distinct. A real, gated Lean Task keeps its input even after the last host lease is released. C reports stale, wrong-kind, wrong-domain, wrong-thread and post-fork uses without consuming a valid owner.

Typed EIO factory rejection and a terminal typed pull failure each deliver an owned resource. A successful task/item delivers an independent lease. The consumers distinguish exhaustion, early close, cooperative cancellation and a non-cooperative late return; an occupied C output is rejected without consuming the pending result.

Each real Ticket owns a /dev/null file descriptor. The runtime's live-identity count and independently observed OS descriptors return to baseline. Retirement rejects further calls but releases live resources and cursors without invoking a new application close effect.

C++ co_await, typed exceptions, move-only ownership, explicit clone, identity comparison across different generated namespaces, deferred worker-thread destruction and dispatcher shutdown are exercised by the installed consumer.

Fresh compilation rejects scalar-erased identities and resources hidden inside copied Except payloads. Changing a transitive input to the declaring module rejects the previous review; changing an unrelated application function preserves the nominal identity.

consumers.output: C leases: identity across packages, typed failures, cancellation and cleanup passed
C++ leases: shared nominal types, typed errors, co_await and owner-thread cleanup passed

replay: With the original handoffs and c-client/ and cpp-client/ directories, set LEAN_BRIDGE_TASK_RESOURCE_REPLAY to their absolute parent and run node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/helpers/resource-task-installed.mjs. This mode verifies and installs the existing archives, with no Lean compiler or producer build.
scope: Compiler-verified, direct application-owned heap resources in the Linux C/C++ task profiles. This does not establish arbitrary resource-bearing sums, host callbacks on Lean workers, all-profile async or trap handling, or a hosted CI run.
